divergences.name: TextPacket
divergences.reason: Control-layout conflict with identical bytes: both 1.26.60 sources model the category byte as the var_u32 selector of a three-way body union whose cases start with the u8 message type, while the protocol 2225 Text marshal writes the category and type as two u8 bytes and dispatches on the type. divergences.name: InventorySlotPacket
divergences.reason: Wire conflict: Mojang declares Container Id as uint8, and 8- and 16-bit fields are fixed-width regardless of Compression, while the protocol 2225 InventorySlot marshal writes WindowID as var_u32. The encodings agree below 128, so the fork is the suspect side. ItemInstance extra-data also shows the extractor limitation recorded for 12 and 15.
divergences.what_would_settle_it: A capture of an InventorySlot packet with a container ID of 128 or above.

divergences.name: CraftingDataPacket
divergences.reason: Modeling limitation: the canonical shaped-recipe ingredient (Endstone cerealizer<RecipeIngredient>::SerializedData) is a var_u32-counted string-to-string map followed by zigzag aux value and count, while the protocol 2225 ItemDescriptorCount and CloudburstMC readIngredient write a var_u32 descriptor kind, a descriptor-name string, a payload chosen by that name, then the zigzag count. The map is byte-identical for the default and invalid descriptors and diverges for molang and item-tag descriptors. A descriptor discriminated by a string is not expressible in the claim format, so no correction is possible without a manifest schema extension.
divergences.what_would_settle_it: A manifest node kind for string-discriminated unions, or evidence that only default descriptors occur in CraftingData at protocol 2225.
